🇦🇪 🚨 UAE — "EMIRATES CUSTOMS eKYC" IDENTITY DATA ALLEGEDLY FOR SALE ALONGSIDE TWO CORPORATE DATASETS

A threat actor on a Russian-language cybercrime forum is selling three datasets it says it obtained first-hand, with the most expensive described as an Emirates Customs eKYC system, priced at US$25,000.

The actor claims:
• Emirates Customs eKYC: 239,226 database documents across 87 collections of Emirates ID / passport-class corporate identity records, about 80 GB of objects, a 25 GB application file tree, an invoice-financing database and bank-channel TLS/PFX certificates
• A US and Latin America freight forwarder ($5,000): 8,102 client companies, invoices, source code and API/JWT/TLS/SSH keys
• A US AI video surveillance and verification platform ($3,500): HubSpot CRM data, recorded videos, evidence files and an AWS account with Terraform states

No samples or proof files were posted. The claim has not been independently verified.

⚠️ Analyst Note:
eKYC identity records and bank-channel certificates would be highly sensitive for a customs and trade-finance environment in the UAE. The seller says current access comes "for free" with the data but is not guaranteed. None of the organizations is clearly named beyond the "Emirates Customs" label, and none has confirmed an incident.

🇺🇸 MAJOR U.S. BANKS REPORT WIDESPREAD SERVICE OUTAGES

Customers at JPMorgan Chase, Bank of America, U.S. Bank, Wells Fargo, Truist and other major financial institutions reported problems accessing online and mobile banking on Monday, according to Downdetector. Chase had the most reports, nearly 4,800 as of 2 p.m. ET, including trouble viewing balances and completing transfers. Bank of America customers also reported ATM problems. Zelle saw a spike in complaints; the payments network said its service was operating normally and that delays may be tied to issues at participating banks. Capital One said it has not been affected.

A Chase spokesperson said the disruption is a technical issue, not a cyber incident, and that customers still have access to their accounts and funds, though some transactions are taking longer than usual. U.S. Bank said its systems were not directly impacted, but Zelle payments sent to or from other institutions may be delayed. No official source has confirmed a cyberattack.
